excerpt: Varda Space Industries flies small capsules that process materials, such as drug crystals, in orbit and return them to Earth. It raised a $187M Series C in 2025.
content:
Varda Space Industries describes itself as a microgravity-enabled life sciences company that processes materials in orbit and returns them to Earth. It builds its W-Series spacecraft and reentry capsules in-house. The idea, as CNBC explained, is that drug ingredients can crystallise differently without gravity, which could lead to new formulations that are hard to make on the ground. Varda's site lists three markets: biopharma companies interested in microgravity crystallisation, microgravity research, and government customers who use the capsules as a hypersonic testbed for reentry and orbital flight testing. Its contact page gives an address in El Segundo, California.

Varda's first mission, W-1, launched in June 2023 on a SpaceX rideshare and grew crystals of the HIV drug ritonavir in orbit. After waiting for a commercial reentry licence from the US Federal Aviation Administration, the capsule landed at the Utah Test and Training Range in February 2024, which Space Explored reported as a first for a commercial company. Rocket Lab built the spacecraft buses for several missions. At the time of its 2025 raise, CNBC reported that Varda had completed three launch-and-return missions, with a fourth in orbit; its website has since announced the launch of W-8 and W-9.

Funding

On 10 July 2025 Varda announced a $187 million Series C led by Natural Capital and Shrug Capital, with Founders Fund, Peter Thiel, Khosla Ventures, Caffeinated Capital, Lux Capital and others, bringing total funding to $329 million. CEO Will Bruey said the money would raise flight cadence and build out a pharmaceutical lab. Fierce Pharma reported that Varda had opened a 10,000-square-foot lab in El Segundo to work on crystallising biologics such as monoclonal antibodies.

Pricing

Varda does not publish prices. Missions and research partnerships are arranged by contacting its biopharma, government or research teams.

This page draws on Varda's website and on CNBC, Fierce Pharma, Space Explored and Rocket Lab's announcements.
